title: Correctness of Shamir sharing
statement: Let $F$ be a field and let $k>0$. In the Shamir scheme over $F$, parties are the nonzero elements of $F$, and sharing a secret $\mathrm{sec}$ with randomness $q$ gives each party the value at its label of the polynomial $\mathrm{sec}+Xq$, where $q$ has degree less than $k-1$. Reconstruction from a set $A$ of parties evaluates at zero the polynomial interpolating their shares; for every set $A$ with at least $k$ elements, every secret, and every randomness value, this reconstruction returns the secret.
hypotheses_covered: The authorized party sets have cardinality at least $k$
The claim holds for every secret and every randomness value
